wv_smoke_hole_canyon.blurb: Smoke Hole Canyon is a limestone gorge carved by the South Branch of the Potomac River, inside Monongahela National Forest between Franklin and Petersburg. Sport climbing dominates, with a smaller share of trad and a stray boulder problem or top-rope. Grades start around 5.7 and reach 5.13, with the heaviest concentration from 5.8 to 5.10 and a solid group of 5.11s and 5.12s above that. Most of the bolted lines can be done with six to ten quickdraws. Guide Wall holds the most climbs, followed by Entrance Walls, Long Branch Wall and Copperhead Cove.

co_lime_park_a_k_a_lime_creek.blurb: Lime Park, also known as Lime Creek, is a limestone canyon in the Eagle area of Colorado, up a dirt road past Sylvan Lake State Park at roughly 9,100 feet. Every climb here is sport, mostly 5.10 to 5.12 with 5.11 the most common grade, plus a smaller group of moderates and a few 5.13s. The limestone is hard and solid, and new routes have been added since development started in the early to mid nineties. The Punchbowl sits on the east side of the canyon and holds the most climbs; The Prow, Blank Check Wall and The Schoolyard are among the crags on the west side.

co_lower_dream_canyon.blurb: Lower Dream Canyon runs along North Boulder Creek in Boulder Canyon, near Boulder, at about 7,100 feet. Boulder jumbles and talus sit at the base of its walls. Sport and trad are split almost evenly, with a modest number of boulder problems, and the grades centre on 5.10 to 5.12 with a few 5.9s and 5.13s at the edges. Plotinus Wall holds the most climbs, followed by Krishna West and Wall of Winter Warmth. At Wall of Winter Warmth the rock is granite, steep and featured, and routes there go up to four pitches.

co_sport_park_the.blurb: The Sport Park sits at the far end of Boulder Canyon, about 12.5 miles up the canyon and roughly 2.5 miles below Nederland, at around 8,000 feet. Boulder Canyon's walls are granite. Sport routes make up most of the climbing, with a smaller number of trad lines, and most sport routes can be top-roped from above. Grades are mostly 5.10 to 5.12, with a good set of 5.8s and 5.9s. The area gets plenty of afternoon sun and can be windy. The south face of Surprising Crag is usually sunny, while the Clock Tower gets morning shade. The Clock Tower and Surprising Crag hold the most climbs.
